tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

{"id":"ENG-2258","uuid":"c4d74691-5123-494f-b478-8137a1c9ef0e","title":"Create a discourse relation from canvas and associate it with the selected node type pair","description":"## Problem

* Users must leave the canvas and navigate to Settings to define a new discourse relation.

## Solution

* Add a canvas dialog that creates a discourse relation with label, complement, and color, and associates it with the active node-type pair.

## Done When

* `Create new` opens the dialog.
* Label, complement, and color can be submitted.
* Submission creates the discourse relation and associates it with the active node types.
* The new relation appears in the relation type menu without a page refresh.
* “Relation type created” and “Discourse relation added” toasts appear.

## Out of Scope

* Full Settings management for discourse relations.
* Managing associations for other node-type pairs.

Continue creates the type, links it to the pair through the ENG-2257 helper, refreshes the menu and shows two toasts. ENG-2259 was merged into this ticket. This PR also carries the end-to-end verification for the parent ticket, ENG-2255. ## Goal / scope agreement - The overall plan and shared decisions are in `AI_sessions/eng-2255-implement-canvas-relation-creation-for-unconfigured-node/_context.md`. Read it first. - Design: DES-349 Case 2 mockup. The dialog is titled "Add relation type" with placeholders "Label (e.g., supports)" and "Complement (e.g., is supported by)", a colour dropdown defaulting to Black, and Cancel / Continue buttons. - **Out of scope:** full relation management in Settings, and linking types to other node-type pairs. ## Approved plan ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Create new"] --> B[CreateRelationTypeModal
label / complement / color] --> C[validate: required + no duplicate label/complement] C --> D[push DiscourseRelationType generateUid 'rel'] --> E[ENG-2257 associate helper] --> F[saveSettings once] --> G[refresh menu + 2 toasts] ``` - Extract `ColorPicker` from `RelationshipTypeSettings.tsx` into a shared component, for example `components/ColorPicker.tsx`. Settings imports it and behaves exactly as before. - Extract the label/complement validation into a pure function (required fields, duplicate label, duplicate complement). Settings behaviour stays the same. Don't tighten the matching (trim or case) unless you flag it as a separate decision. - New dialog: an Obsidian `Modal` with a `createRoot` React root, following `ModifyNodeModal`. Pass it `plugin`, the pair and an `onCreated` callback. Show errors with the existing `input-error` / `text-error text-xs` classes. - On Continue: 1. Build `{ id: generateUid("rel"), label, complement, color, created, modified }` with no `status`. 2. Associate the type with the pair through the ENG-2257 helper, saving only once if possible. 3. Close the dialog, refresh the dropdown list, and show both toasts: "Relation type created", then "Discourse relation added" with description `{label} relation added for {source type} and {target type}`. - Dropdown and overlay: while the dialog is open, the dropdown's capture-phase `window` `pointerdown` and Escape listeners must do nothing. Otherwise a click or Escape in the modal dismisses the menu and **deletes the pending arrow**. Use a ref flag checked in both listeners, or skip events whose target is inside `.modal-container`. When the dialog is cancelled, the arrow and menu stay open. ship_when_verified: no ## Key decisions - **[2026-09-27] ENG-2259 was merged into this ticket.** *Why:* DES-349 Case 2 is one flow, and creating a type without associating it is a dead end. Linear is updated: new title and Done When, and ENG-2259 is a Duplicate. - **[2026-09-27] Use an in-canvas dialog, not a redirect to Settings.** This is John's call on DES-349; later changes will follow user feedback. - **[2026-09-27] Cancelling the dialog keeps the arrow and the menu.** - **[2026-09-27] After Continue, the menu returns to the list view.** Don't apply the new type automatically; this matches the Case 2 mockup, step 3. ## Constraints & preferences - **Base branch:** straight after `/start`, before any commits, run `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/eng-2257-add-an-existing-discourse-relation-from-relation-menu`, or use the local branch. Open the PR against the ENG-2257 branch. `/create-pr` reads its target branch from the main checkout, so check it before pushing. - The target size is 400 lines or fewer, excluding tests. If it goes over, the Reviewer brief must explain why the PR can't be split. - Code comments are one or two lines at most. Don't add single-use wrapper functions. - Before review, run `dg-pr-adherence-check` and `scope-check`. ## Gotchas / landmines - [2026-09-27] ENG-2328, stacked on ENG-2256, raises the dropdown root's z-index to between 301 and 399 so it sits above the style panel. The dropdown's `window` capture listener runs **before** the modal handles Escape, so the guard has to be in the dropdown. - The Obsidian 1.13 `.setting-item` card and the Tailwind preflight gaps apply if Settings markup is used inside the modal. - Another worktree's dev watcher can overwrite the vault plugin build. Grep the bundle before trusting a CDP run. - In CDP, tldraw ignores programmatic `store.put` for autosave, so drive real pointer and keyboard input. ## Current state Not started. It's blocked until the ENG-2257 branch exists; ENG-2256 is done (PR #1491). What ENG-2256 built that this ticket depends on: - `Create new` is a button with no `onClick`, in the shared `addActions` fragment that renders in both the empty state and the "+" flyout. - The dropdown's Escape handler closes the flyout first, using `stopPropagation` in the window capture listener, and then dismisses the menu. The "ignore while the dialog is open" guard has to cover this handler and the outside-click `pointerdown` handler. - The flyout's open state is the boolean `isAddMenuOpen`. Close the flyout when the dialog opens. ## Next step Reset onto the ENG-2257 branch. Extract `ColorPicker` and the validation, with Settings behaviour unchanged, and then build the modal. ## Verification - Run throwaway scratchpad unit tests for the extracted validation (empty fields, duplicate label or complement) and for building the type plus triple. Don't commit them. - Run `pnpm -C apps/obsidian ci:validate` or the repo equivalent. - Run `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` scenarios: 1. **Empty pair, Create new.** Fill in the dialog → Continue. Both toasts appear, the new type is in the menu without a reload, and picking it creates the relation with the correct colour and arrow text. 2. **Populated pair.** "+" → Create new works the same way. 3. **Validation.** A duplicate label or complement shows an error and saves nothing. 4. **Dialog doesn't dismiss the menu.** Clicking inside the dialog and pressing Escape to close it both leave the pending arrow and the menu in place. Cancel does the same. 5. **Settings regression.** Settings → Relation types: the colour picker and duplicate validation still work, and the new type is listed after the tab remounts. 6. **ENG-2255 end to end.** From a fresh vault with no triples for the pair, go from dragging an arrow → Add existing, and separately → Create new, through to a usable relation. Capture the screenshots for `pr-evidence`. ## Open questions / blockers - None.

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile

- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible

  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --slot 1 --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 vault locked, 3 marker missing.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- Slots come from `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env`. It takes a JSON array or a comma list of plugin dirs or vault roots. `--slot N` is 1-based and defaults to 1.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved slot, the lock and the Obsidian state. If another live run holds the lock, it exits 2 and asks you to switch slot. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about competing `dev.ts`/esbuild watchers. Your own worktree's watcher counts too, if it mirrors into the same vault.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |

input.command:
M=/Users/trang.doan/.claude/projects/-Users-trang-doan-Desktop-code-discourse-graph/memory; cat > $M/reference_obsidian_settings_separate_window.md <<'EOF'
---
name: reference_obsidian_settings_separate_window
description: Obsidian 1.13 opens Settings in its own window; CDP mouse input to the main target can't reach it
metadata:
  type: reference
---
In Obsidian 1.13 (seen on 1.13.7, dgDevVault), `app.setting.open()` renders settings in a separate window ("Settings - <vault> - Obsidian"). `app.setting.activeTab.containerEl` is connected, but not to the main `document`, so `document.querySelector` finds nothing and CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` on the main page target never reaches it.

For a Settings check in a dg-obsidian-cdp-verify scenario, query from `app.setting.activeTab.containerEl` and drive it with DOM events. For inputs, use that window's native value setter plus `input`, then `focusout`. Say so in the scenario's input column. Related: [[reference_obsidian_cdp_driving]].

Also: the "Relation types" tab button in `Settings.tsx` has no `discourse-tab` class (the other tabs do), so select tabs by text.
EOF
cat > $M/reference_obsidian_modal_overflow_clips_popovers.md <<'EOF'
---
name: reference_obsidian_modal_overflow_clips_popovers
description: Obsidian's .modal is overflow:auto, so absolute dropdowns (e.g. ColorPicker) in a short modal get clipped and clicks hit .modal-bg
metadata:
  type: reference
---
Obsidian's `.modal` element has `overflow: auto`. An absolutely positioned popover inside a short modal, such as the relation-type `ColorPicker` list, is clipped to the modal box. Options below the edge only appear if you scroll inside the modal. A click where the option looks to be lands on `.modal-bg` and closes the modal.

Fix used in ENG-2258: `this.modalEl.addClass("overflow-visible")` in `onOpen`. The Tailwind class overrides Obsidian's rule. Check it with `elementFromPoint` on an option's centre.
EOF
cat >> $M/MEMORY.md <<'EOF'
- [reference_obsidian_settings_separate_window.md](reference_obsidian_settings_separate_window.md) — Obsidian 1.13 Settings is a separate window; CDP mouse can't reach it, drive via activeTab.containerEl DOM
- [reference_obsidian_modal_overflow_clips_popovers.md](reference_obsidian_modal_overflow_clips_popovers.md) — .modal is overflow:auto; absolute dropdowns in short modals clip and clicks close the modal — add overflow-visible
EOF

content.text:
ENG-2258 is built and working in Obsidian: all six verification scenarios pass on the dev vault. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works:** `Create new` opens an "Add relation type" dialog with label, complement and colour (default Black). Continue creates the type, links it to the node pair, saves once, returns the menu to the list with the new type, and shows both toasts. While the dialog is open, clicks inside it, Escape, Cancel and clicking the backdrop all leave the menu and the pending arrow alone.

**Two bugs found along the way, both fixed:**
- **Toasts replacing each other:** `showToast` built IDs from `Date.now()`, and tldraw drops any toast with a repeated ID. The two success toasts fire in the same millisecond, so one could silently replace the other. IDs are now unique ([toastUtils.ts](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/toastUtils.ts)).
- **Colour list clipped:** Obsidian's modal box scrolls, which cut off most of the colour list. Clicking a hidden colour landed on the backdrop and closed the dialog. The dialog now lets the list extend past its edge.

**Changes**
- [CreateRelationTypeModal.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/CreateRelationTypeModal.tsx) (new): the dialog. Enter submits, errors use the existing classes, and a failed save shows an error and keeps the dialog open.
- [RelationTypeDropdown.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/overlays/RelationTypeDropdown.tsx): wires up `Create new`. The "Discourse relation added" toast is now one helper shared with "Add existing".
- [relationTypeUtils.ts](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationTypeUtils.ts): `createRelationTypeForNodePair` reuses the ENG-2257 helper and undoes both the new type and the link if the save fails.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. # Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/pr-evidence

# PR evidence upload

Uploads PNGs through `roamAlphaAPI.file.upload` in an authenticated Roam Playwright slot, files them under a page in the slot's graph (`discourse-dev-graph`), and emits a Markdown table that create-pr pastes into the Evidence section.

## When to use

- After verification (Roam `load-extension` run, Obsidian CDP run, manual captures) left PNGs on disk.
- Before create-pr builds the body. Roam PRs: reuse the verification's slot once that run has closed. Obsidian PRs: omit `--slot`.

## Command

Run from the worktree root, using the worktree's own `tsx` so the relative PNG paths and the repo's Playwright resolve:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts \
  [--slot N] [--branch <b>] [--label "<YYYY-MM-DD · shortsha · harness>"] [--harness <name>] \
  [--out table.md] [--settle-ms 5000] \
  shot1.png="Empty state" shot2.png="After import" ...
```

- `pnpm --filter roam exec tsx ...` also works, but it changes cwd to `apps/roam`, so pass absolute PNG paths.
- `--branch` defaults to the current git branch. `--label` defaults to `<today> · <short sha> · <--harness or "manual">`.
- Caption defaults to the file name without extension.
- No `--slot`: tries each configured slot (1, 2, 3) and moves on only on a profile-lock error.
- Headless by default (`HEADLESS=false` to watch).

## Output contract

- stdout: JSON `{page, pageUid, branchBlockUid, runBlockUid, items: [{caption, url, blockUid}]}`.
- stderr: `Markdown table: <path>`. The file defaults to `pr-evidence-<runBlockUid>.md` next to the first PNG and contains `| Scenario | Screenshot |` rows with `![caption](url)`. create-pr pastes it as-is.
- URLs are public Firebase storage links (`200 image/png` without cookies, verified 2026-09-23).

## Roam structure

```
Trang test/                       (page, found or created)
  <branch>                        (top-level block, reused on every run)
    <date · sha · harness>        (new run block per invocation, appended last)
      <caption> ![](<url>)        (one per PNG)
```

## Gotchas

- Imports `apps/roam/scripts/playwright/roamSession.ts` from the current worktree (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), so profiles live in that worktree's `local/roam-playwright/profiles/` unless `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<n>` is set.
- A slot's profile can only be open once. Close the verification session first, never delete lock files.
- Login errors (expired session, 2FA) come from `openRoamSession`; recover with `pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot N --headed --allow-login`, then rerun.
- Never print values from `apps/roam/.env`.
- Uploads cannot be rolled back and Roam cannot list graph files, so don't loop retries on a failing run.
- tsx injects `__name()` into functions passed to `page.evaluate`; the script shims it in the page first. Keep that shim if you edit the in-page code.

The ENG-2258 PR is open and ready for review: [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1494](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1494).

- **Base:** `eng-2257-add-an-existing-discourse-relation-from-relation-menu`, because this branch is built on it. [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1492](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1492) has to merge first, and it's itself stacked on ENG-2256.
- **Size:** 8 files, +438/−50. Excluding tests it's 344 changed lines, under 400, so no split justification was needed.
- **CI:** 2 checks passing, 1 skipped, none failing so far.
- **Screenshots:** all 6 are uploaded to the Roam dev graph and embedded in the body, and each URL loads publicly.
- **Watching:** the PR is bound to this session and auto-fix is on, so CI failures, merge conflicts and review comments will wake it up. I also recorded the current comments as the baseline for the scheduled comment sweep, so it won't re-send them.

The only item left in the body is the Loom, still marked `pending`. Here's a shot list, about 90 seconds, one shot per results row:

1. **Empty pair (20s).** Open `_verify/eng-2256-implement-new-relation-menu-empty-state/relation-menu-canvas`. Drag from Question to Claim, click **Create new**, type a label and complement, pick Blue, click **Continue**. Expect the dialog to close, the menu to list only the new type, and both toasts to appear.
2. **Use it (10s).** Click the new type in the menu. Expect a blue arrow labelled with it.
3. **Populated pair (10s).** Drag from Evidence to Claim, click **+**, then **Create new** in the flyout. Expect the flyout to close as the dialog opens, and the new type to appear after supports and opposes.
4. **Validation (15s).** Click Continue with empty fields, then try "supports " with a trailing space. Expect "Label is required", then `Duplicate label "supports"`, with nothing saved.
5. **Dialog keeps the arrow (15s).** Click inside the dialog and press Escape, then Cancel, then click the backdrop. Expect the menu and pending arrow to stay each time; one more Escape dismisses both.
6. **Settings (10s).** Open Settings → Relation types. Expect the new row in Blue, and the duplicate check working as before.
7. **Worth narrating (10s):**
   - While the dialog is open, the menu deliberately ignores outside clicks and Escape.
   - The toast ID fix also affects every other canvas toast.

Run `/checkpoint` if you want to save this session's context before wrapping up.

content.text:
I fixed and pushed both bugs Devin flagged on [DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph#1494](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1494) (commit `e360e20a`), and replied in and resolved both threads.

- **Duplicate types from a stale list:** the dialog checked for duplicates against the relation types it had when it opened. If another canvas added a type meanwhile, you could save a duplicate, and Settings would then refuse later edits. The dialog now reads the current list from settings at the moment you submit.
- **Escape during a save:** Escape or clicking the backdrop could close the dialog mid-save. The type was saved anyway, which looked like a cancel that didn't happen. The dialog now ignores both while a save is running and closes once the save finishes, so the menu also refreshes after the save rather than before.

Both fixes are in `CreateRelationTypeModal.tsx`, plus a one-line change in `RelationTypeDropdown.tsx`.

**Verification:**
- All 8 Obsidian scenarios pass, including two new ones for these fixes:
  - A type saved to settings while the dialog is open is now rejected as a duplicate, and only one copy exists.
  - With the save slowed to 1.5 seconds, Escape and a backdrop click leave the dialog open until the save finishes. It then closes, lists the new type and shows both toasts.
- The 50 unit tests, type-check and lint all pass.
- I didn't run the two new scenarios against the old code to watch them fail first.

I added the two new rows to the PR body's results table and noted Devin's findings in the review section. Auto-fix is still on for CI failures and further comments.
